subject: Service continuity recap and verification plan for Suncrest
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Harper <elliot.harper@suncrestbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service continuity recap and verification plan for Suncrest

Hi Elliot / Suncrest ops team,

Thanks again for the patience while we completed our internal analysis. Attached is a concise post-incident packet (suncrest_rca.pdf) and an excerpt of the KV cache logs we referenced (kv_log_excerpt.txt). Below is a short non-technical summary plus the technical timeline and concrete next steps we will execute with your ops team for verification.

Executive summary (what happened)
- On 2026-09-07 00:45 UTC we observed an elevated error rate and tokenization mismatches for requests routed to a subset of Dedicated nodes serving your account.
- Root cause: a race condition in the autoscaling controller caused a small group of workers to be restarted while their local prefix/KV cache state was still being used by in-flight sessions, leading to inconsistent KV lookups and degraded model responses (5xx and incorrect completions). This is a rare interaction between scale-out and our session affinity logic.

Impact
- Service: intermittent 5xx errors and increased tail latency for ~37 minutes for ~2.4% of requests routed to the affected dedicated pool.
- Data: no customer data was exfiltrated. The issue affected inference session state only; there is no evidence of persisted customer data leakage.

Technical timeline (UTC)
- 2026-09-07 00:43 — Synthetic monitoring alert: increased 5xx rate from pool eu-west-1-dedicated-7 (routing tier).
- 2026-09-07 00:45 — Automated routing fallback engaged; approx 45% of affected traffic rerouted to warm fallback variants.
- 2026-09-07 00:48 — Ops observed continued tokenization mismatch errors from a subset of worker nodes; manual isolation of nodes began.
- 2026-09-07 01:17 — Temporary mitigation: full pool restart and forced cache invalidation for affected hosts. Errors drop to baseline by 01:25.
- 2026-09-07 03:05 — Hotfix deployed to the autoscaler that prevents in-flight cache usage during scale events; canary validated at 03:30.

Immediate customer-facing remediation done
- Forced invalidation of prefix/KV caches for your dedicated pool.
- Controlled rollout of autoscaler guard to prevent concurrent restart+session affinity collisions.
- Increased synthetic coverage for sequence integrity checks in your routing path.

Action items and timeline (what we will do next)
1) Within 48 hours: deliver the full evidence bundle and logs to your secure drive link (attached). Responsible: David Kim.
2) Within 5 business days: run a jointly observed verification test suite with your ops team (we propose 2026-09-10 or 2026-09-11). Responsible: Marissa Cole + Suncrest ops.
3) Within 10 business days: deploy an additional safety guard in the serving runtime to prefer cold cache invalidation during safe drain windows (engineering ETA: 2026-09-17). Responsible: Runtime team (Hannah Schmitt).
4) Post-mitigation: review SLA credit eligibility once verification completes; we will propose credits as appropriate. Responsible: Markus (customer advocate) + Billing.

Requested next steps from Suncrest
- Confirm a preferred verification window (we suggested 2026-09-10/11).
- Confirm whether you want a dedicated post-verification call (30-45 minutes) or only asynchronous sign-off.

Attachments: suncrest_rca.pdf (detailed causal analysis), kv_log_excerpt.txt (redacted logs).

If you prefer a short walkthrough this afternoon I can join — otherwise we'll await your preferred verification window and proceed with the evidence upload.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: suncrest_rca.pdf (26 pages, redacted), kv_log_excerpt.txt (1.2MB, redacted excerpt)

2) SLA credits — will Redwood proactively propose a credit or do we start the request after verification?
3) Verification window — 2026-09-10 morning PT works for us; please confirm a 9:00–10:00 PT slot.

If you can answer 1–2 quickly we can lock the window and prepare our ops folks. Appreciate the thoroughness.

—Elliot

Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 10:00:00 -0700

Elliot — short answers here plus proposed verification steps. I'm copying Hannah and David for technical specifics and the action tracker (attached).

1) Data exposure: Our forensics team completed an audit of logs and replication paths. No raw inference request payloads or PII-bearing metadata were forwarded to any third-party service during the event. The affected artifacts were in-memory session state and local cache shards; we have confirmed no writes to durable customer stores. The attached evidence bundle includes access logs and a redaction map.

2) SLA credits: We will open a credit evaluation with billing now and will present a recommended credit at the post-verification sign-off meeting. If you prefer a preliminary estimate sooner, Billing can provide an indicative figure prior to the verification completion.

3) Verification window: We confirm 2026-09-10 09:00–09:45 PT for the jointly observed test. Meeting invite will be sent by Marissa.

Planned verification agenda (30–45 minutes)
- 5 min: executive overview and objectives
- 15 min: live replay of the synthetic integrity checks and focused traffic tests (we will run your test set and a mirrored synthetic load)
- 10 min: evidence review (logs, cache invalidation traces)
- 5–15 min: agree on closure criteria and next steps

Action tracker (attached): suncrest_action_tracker.xlsx — includes owners and deadlines.

If anything urgent pops up before the 10th, Hannah is available to join a technical call to walk through the log slices.

Thanks — Markus

---

We reviewed the packet and the evidence links you uploaded. The audit note on no PII persistence addresses our primary concern — appreciate the thoroughness. We confirm the verification slot on 2026-09-10 09:00 PT and will have our platform and compliance engineers on the call.

A couple of asks before close: 
- Please confirm when the final evidence bundle (full redacted logs) will be available on the drive link — we want to pull the logs for our internal retention process.
- Please include the expected SLA credit estimate in the post-verification notes so we can brief our procurement team.

Assuming the verification proceeds as planned, Suncrest will accept the remediation and close the incident once we have the sign-off artifact.

Appreciate the responsiveness and the clear owners.
